assets.name: service-countersink
assets.prompt:
Use case: product-mockup. Asset type: square 1254 by 1254 pixel premium architectural-glass machining catalogue sample photograph. Photorealistic studio macro photography of a single understandable machining operation, illustrative glass sample, not a branded SKU or factory scene. Warm neutral greige limestone tabletop, soft lateral neutral daylight, clean off-white studio backdrop, restrained shadows. The machining feature fills most of the frame and is instantly readable. Ultra-clear low-iron CrystalVision glass: every glass surface, machined feature and edge must be colorless neutral white/silver/gray; absolutely NO green, cyan, teal, turquoise, blue or colored glass edges, reflections, ambient light. No objects or plants reflected in glass. Real credible solid glass geometry, precise machining, realistic thickness. NO words, text, logos, labels, diagrams, illustrations, callouts, rulers, dimension marks, dotted lines, laser glow, tools, hands, people, factory clutter, collage or multiple views.
Subject: One thick rectangular optically neutral clear glass plate, lying flat on warm greige stone, close angled three-quarter macro shot. The subject is ONE circular through-hole in the glass with a visibly recessed CONICAL COUNTERSINK around it on the upper face. A broad circular opening tapers smoothly downward in a short 45-degree conical ring to the smaller circular cylindrical through-hole at its center. Make the sloping conical interior surface and its circular upper and lower rims unambiguous in the light, clearly carved INTO the glass, not a ring or part placed on top. Show the lower exit of the through-hole and the stone underneath subtly through the hole. The slab is about 12mm thick, polished flat upper face. Hole is located away from the outer edges; the image contains only ONE countersunk hole, no screw or metal fitting. Tight high-resolution macro, conical cavity large and legible.
assets.visualInspection: Actual image inspected: one through-hole with broad conical recessed ring and smaller cylindrical exit; transparent neutral-color slab, no metal insert.
assets.colorInspection: Inspected actual photo: neutral white/silver/gray clear-glass edges; no green tint.

Subject: Two thick optically clear rectangular glass sample parts arranged as a simple right-angle L corner on a warm neutral stone studio plinth. The parts represent panels prepared for an architectural 90-degree corner joint: EACH meeting END EDGE is cut across the FULL THICKNESS at precisely 45 degrees, so the two opposed 45-degree mitred edge planes together form a right angle. This is a through-thickness 45-degree MITRE CUT, NOT a decorative wide bevel border on the face. The two sample parts are slightly separated by a narrow 3mm gap at the joint so both clean diagonal full-thickness cut planes can be seen and understood. Camera high oblique close view down toward the end of the L joint, exposing rectangular glass faces, thickness, the two simple flat diagonal meeting planes and the sharp outside corner they would form when closed. Approximately 12mm glass thickness, polished faces, neutral white-gray edge highlights. Only two parts, no extra block, no holes, no metal.
assets.visualInspection: Actual final image inspected: two separate rectangular clear samples each with a full-thickness 45-degree sloping end face and visible triangular side profile; not a shallow decorative face bevel. Samples shown before joint assembly.
assets.colorInspection: Inspected actual photo: neutral white/silver/gray clear-glass edges; no green tint.
correctionPrompts: Use case: precise-object-edit. Correct ONLY the geometry of the two meeting end edges of these two transparent glass sample panels. They must be a true 45-degree MITRE JOINT for a 90-degree L corner, not square-cut end faces. Remove a triangular wedge across the entire thickness of EACH end so each end face is diagonal at 45 degrees to its panel face. Keep the two panels themselves at exactly 90 degrees to one another. At their nearly assembled L corner, the two exposed mitred end faces must be PARALLEL TO EACH OTHER and face each other across a narrow even 2 mm gap; they are the two sides of the same diagonal seam. Their common joint plane BISECTS the 90-degree L-corner angle. On the upper visible thickness surfaces, the two diagonal mitre-cut edges must run parallel, one just beside the other, not diverge into a V. The outside tips nearly meet at the outside corner, while the inside tips nearly meet at the inside corner. Show both real full-thickness diagonal cut planes clearly by preserving the small gap and high oblique macro viewpoint. No decorative face bevel. Preserve image style, warm neutral stone plinth, soft light, two rectangular clear glass panels, no other objects. Glass absolutely colorless neutral white/silver/gray, no green/cyan/blue. No text, diagrams, labels, line drawings, arrows. Photorealistic machining sample.

Use case: product-mockup. Corrected new photo for glass service "45-degree full-thickness mitre edge cut". Square 1254x1254 premium macro architectural materials photography, warm greige limestone studio surface, soft neutral sidelight, no text or diagrams. Show TWO SEPARATE SMALL RECTANGULAR CLEAR GLASS OFFCUT SAMPLES laid flat, parallel and staggered diagonally on the stone, not joined together. Each glass piece is a solid thick flat plate about 15mm thick and 100mm across. On EACH piece, the entire FRONT END EDGE has been saw-cut and polished as ONE FLAT 45-DEGREE SLOPING END PLANE ACROSS THE FULL THICKNESS. The top face stops 15mm before the bottom-face edge, creating a sharp tapered glass wedge end. There is NO remaining vertical square-cut end strip, and NO shallow decorative bevel on the top face. The triangular side silhouette of the full-depth 45-degree cut must be clearly visible at the near side corner of each sample, with the sloping plane running from the top surface all the way to the lower sharp tip. These are the two matching mitre-prepared parts before assembly into a right-angle corner. Use a low oblique macro camera looking along the front bevel edge and slightly across the cut side profile so the actual 45° diagonal across thickness is visually unmistakable. One sample nearer and one slightly behind, both cut planes face camera, show at least one square uncut side edge on each piece for thickness comparison. Glass is absolutely colorless transparent low-iron CrystalVision, silver-white and neutral gray edges only, no blue cyan green tint or reflections. Photorealistic realistic glass machining sample, no metal, no etched marks, no tools, no inset image, no illustration, no decorative perimeter bevel frame.
